secrets_stored_in_plaintext.title: Secrets Stored in Plaintext
secrets_stored_in_plaintext.description: Indicates whether the configuration file contains credentials, API keys, tokens, or database passwords stored directly as plaintext values rather than references to a secret manager, environment variables, or encrypted values.

secret_manager_integration.title: Secret Manager Integration Configured
secret_manager_integration.description: Indicates whether the application or configuration file is integrated with a dedicated secret management system (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager) so that secrets are retrieved at runtime rather than embedded in the file.

file_encryption_at_rest.title: Configuration File Encrypted at Rest
file_encryption_at_rest.description: Indicates whether the configuration file itself is encrypted at rest using filesystem-level encryption, an encrypted secrets file format (e.g., SOPS, Ansible Vault), or a similar mechanism that prevents plaintext exposure of embedded values if the file is accessed directly.

classification_label_assigned.title: Data Classification Label Assigned
classification_label_assigned.description: Indicates whether the configuration file (or the directory/repository containing it) has been assigned a formal data sensitivity classification label (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) via metadata, extended attributes, a manifest, or a classification registry entry.

contains_sensitive_values.title: File Contains Sensitive Values
contains_sensitive_values.description: Indicates whether the configuration file contains one or more sensitive values such as credentials, API keys, database connection strings, tokens, or private certificates — determined by static scanning or manual review.

classification_enforcement_mechanism.title: Classification Enforcement Mechanism
classification_enforcement_mechanism.description: Describes the mechanism used to enforce downstream handling controls derived from the classification label, such as access restrictions, encryption mandates, or retention schedules.

world_readable.title: World-Readable Permission Bit Set
world_readable.description: Whether the configuration file has the world (other) read bit set, making it readable by any user on the system regardless of group membership.

group_readable_by_non_operational_group.title: Group-Readable by Non-Operational Group
group_readable_by_non_operational_group.description: Whether the file's group-read bit is set AND the owning group includes users beyond those with a legitimate operational need (i.e., the group is not tightly scoped to the service). True indicates overly broad group read access.

file_owner_matches_service_account.title: File Owner Matches Service Account
file_owner_matches_service_account.description: Whether the file's owning user is the dedicated service account or process account with operational need for the configuration file. True means ownership is correctly scoped.

file_permission_mode.title: File Permission Mode (Octal)
file_permission_mode.description: The octal permission string of the configuration file (e.g., '644', '640', '600'). Reflects read/write/execute bits for owner, group, and others.

stale_config_files_present.title: Stale Configuration Files Present
stale_config_files_present.description: Whether the filesystem contains superseded, deprecated, or backup configuration files (e.g., .env.old, config.bak, settings.bak, .env.backup, web.config.bak) that are no longer operationally active.

retention_policy_defined.title: Configuration File Retention Policy Defined
retention_policy_defined.description: Whether a formal, documented retention and expiry policy exists for configuration files — including backup and superseded copies — specifying maximum retention periods and disposal procedures.

stale_config_contains_secrets.title: Stale Configuration Files Contain Active Secrets
stale_config_contains_secrets.description: Whether any of the identified stale or backup configuration files contain credentials, API keys, database connection strings, or other secrets that are still valid or reusable.

secure_deletion_method_applied.title: Secure Deletion Method Applied
secure_deletion_method_applied.description: Indicates whether a secure deletion or cryptographic erasure method (e.g., shred, srm, cryptographic erase) was applied to retired or decommissioned configuration files rather than standard filesystem deletion.

retired_config_files_recoverable.title: Retired Config Files Are Recoverable
retired_config_files_recoverable.description: Indicates whether retired or replaced configuration files remain recoverable from the filesystem, recycle bin, volume snapshots, or backup stores — meaning they were not securely purged from all storage locations.

disposal_procedure_documented.title: Formal Disposal Procedure Documented
disposal_procedure_documented.description: Indicates whether a formal, enforced disposal procedure exists specifically covering configuration files, requiring secure deletion or cryptographic erasure steps before files are considered retired.

environment_type.title: Environment Type
environment_type.description: The classification of the environment where the configuration file resides (production, staging, development, test).

contains_production_secrets.title: Contains Production Secrets
contains_production_secrets.description: Whether the configuration file contains live production credentials, API keys, database connection strings, or other production-environment secrets rather than placeholder or masked values.

secrets_masked_or_sanitized.title: Secrets Masked or Sanitized
secrets_masked_or_sanitized.description: Whether all sensitive fields in the configuration file have been replaced with placeholder values, environment variable references, or vault references rather than literal secret values.

access_control_equivalent_to_production.title: Access Control Equivalent to Production
access_control_equivalent_to_production.description: Whether file-system and application-level access controls on the configuration file in the lower environment are as restrictive as those applied in production.
